explained.headline: Superpowers hold unprecedented summit in Shenzhen as Crimean Bridge is struck

happened.text: The Crimean Bridge connecting Russia to the occupied peninsula was hit by a combined missile-and-drone strike that destroyed its central road section.

Simultaneously, United States President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin convened for unprecedented trilateral talks on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen.
Following the attacks on the bridge, Russian President Vladimir Putin vowed a response that would be far more painful than Kyiv's strikes.

background.text: Moscow has since used the peninsula as a military base to carry out strikes and resupply its troops in southern Ukraine.
Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

matters.text: Kyiv's defence ministry stated that the bridge strikes amounted to time gained and lives saved by reducing what reaches occupying forces.
Analysts said the trilateral meeting between the US, Russia and China was unlikely to produce major agreements due to deep differences over Ukraine, Iran, nuclear weapons and trade.

uncertain.text: The exact duration of the repairs required for the heavily damaged Crimean Bridge remains unclear, though officials note the work will likely take a long time under frequent fire.
It remains unconfirmed whether concrete steps towards nuclear disarmament will emerge, despite the signed peace declaration mentioning a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks.

explained.headline: International Court of Justice rules Myanmar committed Rohingya genocide

happened.text: The International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya Muslim minority during a 2017 military campaign.
Yuji Iwasawa, president of the court, stated that a majority of nine out of fifteen judges concluded that Myanmar intended to destroy a substantial part of the population.

background.text: The case was brought to the court in 2019 by Gambia, a West African nation, on behalf of Rohingya survivors.
Myanmar's leadership denied carrying out genocide, claiming the military operations were legitimate counter-terrorism measures against armed insurgents.

matters.text: The decision marks the first time the International Court of Justice has found a sovereign state responsible for genocide.
Britain's foreign minister, Ed Miliband, announced the expulsion of Myanmar's defence attaché and called for an urgent session at the United Nations Security Council.
Observers note that the ruling could serve as a vital precedent for other high-profile genocide cases before the court, including allegations concerning actions in Gaza.

uncertain.text: Sources note that the International Court of Justice lacks direct enforcement powers, leaving the practical impact dependent on future international actions such as sanctions or Security Council measures.
It remains unclear whether Myanmar will comply with the court's orders to provide reparations, facilitate safe returns, and investigate wrongdoing.

terms.definition: The principal judicial organ of the United Nations that settles legal disputes between states.
An international treaty that criminalises genocide and obligates signatory states to prevent and punish the crime.

removed.text: The 2016-2017 military operations drove more than 700,000 Rohingya across the border into Bangladesh, where many remain in large refugee settlements.
Judges found that security forces killed thousands of civilians, carried out widespread sexual violence and extreme violence against children, and restricted births.
why: Evidence mentions killing 10,000, while the claim says thousands; it does not confirm the claim's 'restricted births' detail.

explained.headline: United States and Venezuela sign military agreement in Caracas

happened.text: The United States and Venezuela have re-established military ties by signing a military co-operation agreement in Caracas.
US Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth travelled to Venezuela and met with interim President Delcy Rodríguez at the presidential palace.

background.text: Relations between Washington and Caracas deteriorated under Hugo Chávez and his successor, Nicolás Maduro, before hitting rock bottom last year.
In January, United States forces seized Nicolás Maduro during a military raid on the capital, Caracas.
Delcy Rodríguez, formerly Nicolás Maduro's vice-president, became acting president with the blessing of United States President Donald Trump.

matters.text: Pete Hegseth stated that Venezuela has transformed from an aggressive regional threat into a compliant security partner.
Pete Hegseth claimed that a related energy agreement will make the Strait of Hormuz an irrelevant factor for the Western Hemisphere.

uncertain.text: Very few specific details about the newly signed military agreement have been published by either government.
It remains unclear when elections might take place in Venezuela following the ouster of Nicolás Maduro.

explained.headline: Israeli forces complete ground operation in central Gaza

happened.text: The Israeli military carried out a ground operation in central Gaza that crossed the yellow line boundary into territory controlled by Hamas.

background.text: The conflict began following an attack led by Hamas on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, which resulted in about 1,200 deaths.
A fragile ceasefire agreement was reached in October 2025, establishing a yellow line that separates Israeli-occupied areas from territory controlled by Hamas.
Despite the truce, violence and military strikes have continued intermittently over the subsequent months.

matters.text: Hamas condemned the incursion as a flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement and a dangerous escalation.
The Board of Peace overseeing the ceasefire warned that a truce delivering no visible improvements cannot be sustained indefinitely and remains at risk of collapse.

uncertain.text: Sources note ongoing disputes over whether both sides have honoured their commitments to end hostilities.
It remains unresolved whether the disarmament of Hamas, a key sticking point in negotiations, can be achieved alongside a phased withdrawal of Israeli troops.

why: Evidence mentions fleeing families, but does not confirm their homes were along the Salah al-Din road.

why: The evidence confirms the operation's goal and completion, but does not mention the area being reopened.
